In summary, human taste and creative judgment have become the scarce resource in an AI-enabled economy, since production capabilities are now widely available and what distinguishes meaningful work is the point of view and discernment behind it.

## Suggested Topics

Generative AI and creativity, AI in marketing, Taste and authenticity

## Matched Topics

[[Generative AI]], [[Content Production]], [[Strategy]]

## Headlines

- **Human taste is now the competitive advantage in an AI economy.** As generative AI tools commoditise production capabilities, the ability to discern what is worth making—and the creative judgment to execute it—has become the defining scarcity.

- **Consumers increasingly distrust AI-generated content that appears too polished.** A Harris Poll found 78% of consumers say AI makes ads feel less authentic, and 73% are less likely to trust ads they suspect were AI-made, signalling that imperfection has become a marker of human involvement.

- **Brands must prioritise showing the human creative process over speed and polish.** Building intimacy through smaller communities, rewarding curiosity with hidden details, and allowing imperfection to signal human craftsmanship are more effective than chasing maximum reach.

- **Physical, community-based experiences are becoming status symbols as digital content saturates.** Gen Z now attends cinemas more frequently than older generations, silent book clubs have expanded to 2,000 chapters across 60 countries, and closed communities are valued precisely because they resist being shared online.

- **The best AI work comes from creators who already possessed refined taste before the tools existed.** AI amplifies existing creative vision rather than replacing judgment; the skill worth building now is knowing which possibilities AI generates actually deserve to exist.

- **People:** Natalie Winford, Thea Cooke-Campbell, Hanna Morra, Chloë Watts, Robert Wong, Will.i.am

- **Places:** The Shard (London), Cannes Lions Festival, SXSW London

Nobody had a definitive answer. Which is kind of the point.
